clue.text: See 4
Misbehave in Scottish island with customised U-boat

parts.note: Muck is a small island in the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: something customised has been altered to suit, so the letters of the vessel are rearranged

parts.note: the submarine's letters, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone causing trouble on a Hebridean island with a modified German submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: Muck is one of the Small Isles off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To muck about is a colloquial phrasal verb for messing around or behaving badly.

clue.text: Freeholder with ace houses on river

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on something means coming directly above it
to house something is to give it a home inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an ace counts as one in cards and dice
W is a standard abbreviation for with
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A property owner with a top-class house by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a joining word but is itself wordplay, the standard abbreviation; 'ace' is the card worth one.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeholder holds land outright, so is its owner rather than a tenant.

clue.text: Endless ale drunk — wind reportedly trapped

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so one piece sits within the other
drunk means unsteady and muddled, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so we want a word that sounds like the given one

parts.note: to wind is to turn; the seabird tern is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: Beer drunk endlessly while suffering trapped wind, a pub complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as flatulence in the surface but is the verb meaning turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal has no end, so it is a direct synonym for endless.

clue.text: Strip police officer's authority

parts.note: a DI is a Detective Inspector; the possessive adds S
a mantle is a role of authority passed from one holder to the next

explanation.surface: A police officer is stripped of his authority.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to strip something down, taking it apart piece by piece.

clue.text: Dicky Emery with old duo who partnered 27?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'one who partnered Peter Cook'

indicators.note: dicky means faulty or shaky, so the letters that follow are put in disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dick Emery, the British TV comic, set alongside an old double act.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Emery was a 1960s-70s British sketch comedian, so 'Dicky' looks like his name rather than the signal that the letters are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudley Moore was the comic and musician who formed a celebrated double act with Peter Cook, the answer to 27.

clue.text: Part-time journalist's copy way superior?

indicators.note: superior means placed higher, so in a down entry this piece comes on top

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
a ringer is a close double or imitation

explanation.surface: Asks whether a freelance reporter's written copy is far better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copy' suggests journalism, but here it means a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringer is a freelance reporter paid per piece rather than a staff journalist.

clue.text: Judge a vicious dog possibly detaining Republican

indicators.note: detaining someone holds them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
R abbreviates Republican
a vicious dog might be called a biter; 'possibly' flags the example

explanation.surface: A judge hearing a case about a dangerous dog that held a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone appointed to settle a dispute, the role of a judge.

clue.text: Loyal old prime minister provides direction

parts.note: loyal and true are synonyms
Lord North was British prime minister 1770-82

explanation.surface: A faithful elder statesman giving guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North led the government during the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: True north is the geographic direction towards the North Pole, as opposed to magnetic north.

clue.text: Door found by guard after polling

indicators.note: polling is cutting off the head, as with pollarded trees, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard

explanation.surface: A door watched by a guard after the voting has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polling' looks like voting, but it is the old sense of beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is a way in, such as a door or entrance.

clue.text: Tory sensitive and hopeful

parts.note: Con abbreviates Conservative, a Tory
tender means sore or sensitive

explanation.surface: A thin-skinned, optimistic Tory politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeful is a candidate with a chance, which is what a contender is.

clue.text: See 26
Gunners in retreat pursued by field marshal

indicators.note: being pursued by something means having it come behind, so the next piece follows
troops in retreat go back the way they came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Royal Artillery, the Gunners
a range is a field or extent of land or activity

explanation.surface: Artillery falling back while chased by a field marshal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field marshal' reads as one military rank, but the clue splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal is to arrange people or things in order.

clue.text: Close to 26 10 on a stool that collapses in comedy show

indicators.note: something that collapses falls into a heap, so these letters are thrown into a new order
the close of something is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: 26 is the first name of the actress at 26/10
the answer to 10, the actress's surname
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer perched on a wobbly stool in a comedy show.
explanation.walkthrough: Not Only... But Also was the 1960s BBC sketch show starring Peter Cook and Dudley Moore, linking it to 27 and 4.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a specific BBC comedy series, so 'comedy show' is its category.

clue.text: Dramatist an individual with health issues

parts.note: one person, a single individual
someone ill has problems with their health

explanation.surface: A playwright who suffers from poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill was the American playwright of Long Day's Journey into Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was a Nobel-winning American playwright, an example of a dramatist.

clue.text: Wiring in circle with set broken

indicators.note: broken things fall into pieces, so these letters are put back in another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Faulty wiring in a circuit, with the television set broken.
explanation.definitionFit: The electrics of a building or car are its electrical system, chiefly its wiring.

clue.text: Rent reduction bringing small show of emotion?

parts.note: a rent is a rip or tear
a drop is a fall or reduction

explanation.surface: A landlord's rent cut moving a tenant to quiet emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' reads as money paid to a landlord, but it is the noun for a split.
explanation.definitionFit: A single falling tear is a small visible sign of feeling, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Piano malarkey given order — expert at creating scores?

parts.note: P is the musical marking for piano, softly

indicators.note: putting something in order rearranges it, so the following letters are sorted afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Piano nonsense tidied up by a composer of film scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' and 'scores' suggest music, but the scores are goals in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmaker in football or rugby sets up the chances from which teammates score.

clue.text: Monsieur et Madame in divorce?

definitions.note: French for 'a couple', read as one English word
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a French husband and wife
second meaning: to separate a joined pair

explanation.surface: A French married couple going through a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase 'un couple', run together, is an English word.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple is to detach or separate two things that were joined, as divorce separates a pair.

clue.text: Hard to be involved in onerous movie

indicators.note: being involved in something means being caught up inside it, so one piece goes within

parts.note: testing means demanding or onerous
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: It is hard to take part in an arduous film shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside TESTING after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sting is the 1973 Oscar-winning film starring Paul Newman and Robert Redford.

clue.text: Shout from chasing pack while keeping band together

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: tho is an informal short form of though, meaning while
to ally is to join forces

explanation.surface: A hunting cry heard as the pack stays together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the traditional cry of fox hunters when they sight the quarry.

clue.text: In due course Greek letter seen by a girl

parts.note: so in the sense 'and then', what follows in due course
phi is the 21st letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eventually spotting a Greek character next to a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia is a female first name, from the Greek word for wisdom.

clue.text: Comply with note and watch clock

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to keep to a rule or custom
further meanings: note, watch and clock all mean to notice

explanation.surface: Follow the rules, take note and keep an eye on the time.
explanation.walkthrough: Four meanings in a row: comply with, note, watch and clock (slang for notice) all give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is both to obey a rule and to notice or watch something.

clue.text: Citizen cross having escaped London prison?

indicators.note: something that has escaped is no longer inside, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: Brixton is a prison in south London
a cross is the shape X

explanation.surface: An angry inmate who has broken out of a London jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: A Briton is a British citizen.

clue.text: See 12
Look delighted when consuming right fish

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to beam is to smile broadly
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: Someone smiling as they eat the right fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream is a freshwater or sea fish, an example of the category.

clue.text: East German rook opening strange beak

indicators.note: an opening comes at the start, so these pieces are placed before the next one

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook
Ost is German for east
rum means odd or strange

explanation.surface: An East German bird nicknamed rook opening an odd beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' suggests the bird, but it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostrum is the zoological term for a beak or snout-like projection.

clue.text: Squadron's leader in base where fliers land

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a root is a base or foundation

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An RAF squadron commander at the base where aircraft land.
explanation.walkthrough: Fliers suggest pilots, but here they are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is the perch where birds settle to rest.

clue.text: Ultimately Andy Linden backed outspoken actress

indicators.note: backed here means sent backwards, so the pair is read from right to left
ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the name
the linden is the lime tree
blunt means frank and outspoken

explanation.surface: Supporting actor Andy Linden finally backed a forthright actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Linden is a British actor, so the names look like people rather than a letter and a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Blunt is a British film actress, known for The Devil Wears Prada and A Quiet Place.

clue.text: Comedian indulged favourite chef after some hesitation

indicators.note: after places the following piece before the one just named

parts.note: a pet is a pampered favourite
er is the sound of hesitating
a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: A spoilt favourite chef who pauses before speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Cook was a British satirist and comedian, Dudley Moore's partner.

clue.text: Run poorly? Silly removing spikes at the start!

indicators.note: silly means scatty and muddled, so the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A runner foolishly taking off the spiked shoes before a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' and 'spikes' suggest athletics; 'removing' is not a deletion signal but anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To misgovern is to rule or manage a country badly.

clue.text: Compound from revolutionary secret service

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A rebel's secret service base.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.
